name: OPL (IBM CPLEX)
summary: An algebraic modeling language for mathematical and constraint programming created by Pascal Van Hentenryck at ILOG and now part of IBM ILOG CPLEX Optimization Studio: typed data declarations (ranges, sets, tuples, arrays), decision variables (dvar), objectives and constraint blocks solved by CPLEX or CP Optimizer, with a JavaScript-like IBM ILOG Script for pre/post-processing and flow control.

level_notes.1: IBM Documentation hosts the OPL Language Reference and User's Manuals (pages render via JavaScript, so topic links are not machine-verifiable); Van Hentenryck's 1999 MIT Press book defined the original language.
level_notes.0: Proprietary; only examples and wrappers are public.
level_notes.2: Secondary material is mostly IBM's own manuals and examples (level 1) and textbooks; no open tutorial linked.
